
```{r}
#| label: data
#| include: false
picks <- read_parquet("data/picks.parquet")
roster <- read_parquet("data/roster.parquet")
coaches <- read_parquet("data/coaches.parquet")
```

## 1. Introduction

- A head coach is one voice on a staff of position coaches who may do most
  of the developing, so what the data can support is a statement about
  association: the head coaches under whom a future draftee played.
- This post counts those associations two ways, by the last season before
  the draft and by every season the player played.
- The two ways disagree for roughly half of recent draft picks, and the
  rising share of draftees who transferred explains most of the widening
  disagreement.
- The post then opens the totals up by the positions of the draftees and by
  the school-to-school splits of coaches who moved.

## 2. Data

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-30. The roster
records start in 2010, so this post covers draft classes from 2011 on, and
early classes carry shorter observable careers than late ones. The window
shape drives the first result below.*
:::

### Two ways to count a draftee's head coaches

```{r}
#| label: rules-table
tibble::tribble(
  ~rule                                          , ~what_it_counts                              , ~names ,
  "Last school"                                  , "The player's final season before the draft" ,
  "Whoever finished the product"                 ,
  "Every season"                                 , "Every season the player played, once each"  ,
  "Everyone who oversaw part of the development"
) |>
  kable(
    caption = "The two counting rules. One roster season is enough under either rule."
  )
```

When a school recorded more than one head coach in a season, midseason
changes and interim promotions, all of them are counted, because the claim
is association rather than sole responsibility. Players whose athlete id
is a known recycled id, the same id attached to two different careers, are
excluded.

### How many picks actually get a coach

```{r}
#| label: funnel
picks_2011 <- picks |>
  filter(!is.na(playerId), year >= 2011) |>
  distinct(year, overall, name)
reused <- reused_ids(roster)
# pool of pre-draft roster seasons for every eligible pick: reused twice below
pool <- picks |>
  filter(!is.na(playerId), year >= 2011, !playerId %in% reused) |>
  distinct(playerId, year, overall) |>
  inner_join(
    distinct(roster, playerId, season, team),
    by = "playerId",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  filter(season < year)
last_school <- link_coaches_picks(
  picks,
  roster,
  coaches,
  rule = "last",
  reused = reused
)
every_season <- link_coaches_picks(
  picks,
  roster,
  coaches,
  rule = "any",
  reused = reused
)
```

```{r}
#| label: funnel-table
funnel <- tibble::tribble(
  ~step                                               , ~n                                                                                                      ,
  "Draft picks, 2011 to 2026"                         , nrow(picks |> filter(year >= 2011))                                                                     ,
  "With an athlete id"                                , nrow(picks |> filter(!is.na(playerId), year >= 2011))                                                   ,
  "After excluding recycled ids"                      , nrow(picks |> filter(!is.na(playerId), year >= 2011, !playerId %in% reused) |> distinct(year, overall)) ,
  "With a roster season before the draft year"        , nrow(distinct(pool, year, overall))                                                                     ,
  "With a head coach in their final pre-draft season" , nrow(distinct(last_school, year, overall))
)
funnel |>
  kable(caption = "How many draft picks survive each link step.")
```

The funnel lands at
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * nrow(distinct(last_school, year, overall)) / nrow(picks |> filter(!is.na(playerId), year >= 2011)))`
of id-bearing picks; the residual is players whose pre-draft seasons never
match a season in the coaches data.

```{r}
#| label: funnel-pin
stopifnot(
  nrow(distinct(last_school, year, overall)) >=
    0.85 *
      nrow(picks |> filter(!is.na(playerId), year >= 2011))
)
```

## 3. Results

### Early classes cannot disagree; half of recent picks do

The roster records start in 2010, so a pick in the 2011 draft can show at
most one pre-draft roster season, and under that constraint the two rules
cannot disagree: they are the same coach by construction. Careers lengthen
inside the window as classes move later, and the two rules get room to
diverge.

*Expecting the two counting rules to name the same head coaches for most
draftees.*

```{r}
#| label: overlap
set_overlap <- function(y, o) {
  a <- last_school$coach_id[last_school$year == y & last_school$overall == o]
  b <- every_season$coach_id[every_season$year == y & every_season$overall == o]
  length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
}
keys <- distinct(last_school, year, overall)
ovl <- keys |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(ovl = set_overlap(year, overall)) |>
  ungroup()
by_class <- ovl |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    identical_share = mean(ovl == 1),
    n_picks = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: overlap-fig
#| fig-height: 6
window_mean <- mean(by_class$identical_share[by_class$year >= 2014])
p <- ggplot(by_class, aes(year, identical_share)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = window_mean, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = sprintf(
        "%d: %.0f%% of %d picks",
        year,
        100 * identical_share,
        n_picks
      ),
      group = 1
    ),
    linewidth = 1.2,
    color = "#1b4f8a"
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = sprintf(
        "%d: %.0f%% of %d picks",
        year,
        100 * identical_share,
        n_picks
      )
    ),
    size = 2.4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The two rules disagree on half of recent picks",
    subtitle = "Picks whose two coach sets are exactly identical, by draft class",
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Picks naming the same coach set\nunder both rules",
    caption = "Dashed line: mean over classes 2014 and later. Overlap is an exact set match on coach ids."
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6)
```

The rest of the post works with the 2014 and later classes, where every
draftee's observable career is plausibly complete, and returns to the late
slide with an explanation.

```{r}
#| label: overlap-pin
stopifnot(
  by_class$identical_share[by_class$year == 2011] == 1,
  window_mean > 0.5,
  window_mean < 0.65,
  all(by_class$identical_share[by_class$year >= 2024] < 0.55)
)
```

❌ Does not hold for the classes of 2024 through 2026, where the identical
share sits below 55%. ✅ Holds for the class of 2011, by construction.

### Burrow, Williams, and Ward show exactly where the rules split

The mechanism is easiest to see in individual careers. The last three first
overall picks in the window make a clean set: Joe Burrow, Caleb Williams,
and Cam Ward.

```{r}
#| label: examples
ex_picks <- picks |>
  filter(
    !is.na(playerId),
    name %in% c("Joe Burrow", "Caleb Williams", "Cam Ward")
  ) |>
  distinct(name, year, overall, playerId)
ex_coaches <- bind_rows(
  ex_picks |>
    inner_join(
      last_school |> select(year, overall, coach_name, team, season),
      by = c("year", "overall")
    ) |>
    mutate(rule = "Last school"),
  ex_picks |>
    inner_join(
      every_season |> select(year, overall, coach_name, team, season),
      by = c("year", "overall")
    ) |>
    mutate(rule = "Every season")
) |>
  mutate(entry = sprintf("%s, %s %d", coach_name, team, season)) |>
  group_by(name, rule) |>
  summarise(coaches = paste(entry, collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = c("Last school", "Every season"))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rule, values_from = coaches, names_sort = TRUE)
ex_coaches |>
  kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Draftee",
      "Coach set under the last-school rule",
      "Coach set under the every-season rule"
    ),
    caption = "Coach sets for the last three first overall picks in the window. A season lists every head coach recorded for it, so co-listed coaches all appear."
  )
```

Joe Burrow's last-school set names Ed Orgeron alone; the every-season rule
also names Urban Meyer, under whom Burrow spent four Ohio State seasons
before transferring to LSU. Caleb Williams followed Lincoln Riley from
Oklahoma to USC, yet his every-season set still adds a second name, Bob
Stoops, because the 2021 Oklahoma season records two head coaches. Cam
Ward's last-school set is Mario Cristobal at Miami; the every-season rule
adds Jake Dickert at Washington State, and his Incarnate Word season
predates the coaches coverage.

```{r}
#| label: examples-pin
stopifnot(
  ex_coaches$`Last school`[ex_coaches$name == "Joe Burrow"] ==
    "Ed Orgeron, LSU 2019",
  grepl(
    "Urban Meyer, Ohio State 2014",
    ex_coaches$`Every season`[ex_coaches$name == "Joe Burrow"],
    fixed = TRUE
  ),
  ex_coaches$`Last school`[ex_coaches$name == "Caleb Williams"] ==
    "Lincoln Riley, USC 2023",
  grepl(
    "Bob Stoops",
    ex_coaches$`Every season`[ex_coaches$name == "Caleb Williams"],
    fixed = TRUE
  ),
  ex_coaches$`Last school`[ex_coaches$name == "Cam Ward"] ==
    "Mario Cristobal, Miami 2024",
  grepl(
    "Jake Dickert",
    ex_coaches$`Every season`[ex_coaches$name == "Cam Ward"],
    fixed = TRUE
  )
)
```

### Saban leads both countings, by different margins

```{r}
#| label: top10
library(gt)
top_last <- last_school |>
  filter(year >= 2014) |>
  distinct(year, overall, coach_id, coach_name) |>
  count(coach_id, coach_name, name = "picks", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(rule = "Last school")
top_any <- every_season |>
  filter(year >= 2014) |>
  distinct(year, overall, coach_id, coach_name) |>
  count(coach_id, coach_name, name = "picks", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(rule = "Every season")
bind_rows(top_last, top_any) |>
  mutate(rule = factor(rule, levels = c("Last school", "Every season"))) |>
  group_by(rule) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(rule, rank, coach_name, picks) |>
  gt(row_group_as_column = TRUE) |>
  cols_label(rank = "Rank", coach_name = "Coach", picks = "Draftees") |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = rank) |>
  tab_caption(
    "Top ten coaches by number of draft picks, 2014 classes on. A coach's total spans schools, so these counts describe the coach, not the school-stint."
  )
```

### Each top coach's draftee mix leans a different direction

A coach's total also hides what kind of players leave his program. Grouping
the nineteen recorded positions into eight groups shows the mix behind the
top of the leaderboard.

```{r}
#| label: positions
pos_groups <- c(
  "Quarterback" = "QB",
  "Running Back" = "RB",
  "Fullback" = "RB",
  "Wide Receiver" = "WR/TE",
  "Tight End" = "WR/TE",
  "Offensive Tackle" = "OL",
  "Offensive Guard" = "OL",
  "Center" = "OL",
  "Defensive End" = "DL",
  "Defensive Edge" = "DL",
  "Defensive Tackle" = "DL",
  "Outside Linebacker" = "LB",
  "Inside Linebacker" = "LB",
  "Linebacker" = "LB",
  "Cornerback" = "DB",
  "Safety" = "DB",
  "Place Kicker" = "ST",
  "Punter" = "ST",
  "Long Snapper" = "ST"
)
pos_links <- last_school |>
  filter(year >= 2014) |>
  mutate(pos_grp = unname(pos_groups[position]))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(pos_links$pos_grp)))
pos_totals <- pos_links |>
  count(coach_id, coach_name, name = "n_total")
top_coaches <- pos_totals |>
  arrange(desc(n_total), coach_name) |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  pull(coach_name)
pos_mix <- pos_links |>
  filter(coach_name %in% top_coaches) |>
  count(coach_name, pos_grp, name = "n") |>
  left_join(pos_totals, by = "coach_name") |>
  mutate(coach_name = reorder(coach_name, n_total))
```

```{r}
#| label: positions-fig
#| fig-height: 7
p_pos <- ggplot(pos_mix, aes(y = coach_name, x = n, fill = pos_grp)) +
  geom_col_interactive(aes(
    tooltip = sprintf("%s: %d %s draftees", coach_name, n, pos_grp),
    data_id = pos_grp
  )) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Saban's draftees skew defensive, Ferentz's to the line",
    subtitle = "Position mix of the twelve coaches with the most draftees",
    x = "Draftees",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Position group",
    caption = "Last-school rule. Bar length is the coach's total draftees."
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p_pos, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 7)
```

The position mixes differ across the top coaches. Nick Saban's 99 draftees include 20
defensive backs and 19 defensive linemen but only 4 quarterbacks, while
Kirk Ferentz's 48 lean offensive line, 11 of 48, with a single running
back. Brian Kelly's 19 receivers and tight ends are the largest count of
any offensive position group among the top twelve.

```{r}
#| label: positions-pin
stopifnot(
  pos_totals$n_total[pos_totals$coach_name == "Nick Saban"] == 99,
  pos_mix$n[pos_mix$coach_name == "Nick Saban" & pos_mix$pos_grp == "DB"] == 20,
  pos_mix$n[pos_mix$coach_name == "Kirk Ferentz" & pos_mix$pos_grp == "OL"] ==
    11,
  pos_mix$n[pos_mix$coach_name == "Brian Kelly" & pos_mix$pos_grp == "WR/TE"] ==
    19,
  max(pos_mix$n[
    pos_mix$pos_grp %in%
      c("QB", "RB", "WR/TE", "OL") &
      pos_mix$coach_name != "Brian Kelly"
  ]) <
    19
)
```

### Some coaches' totals split evenly across schools; others do not

Because a coach's total spans schools, the leaderboard cannot say whether
the draftees followed the coach or the program. A handful of the top names
have moved, and their per-school splits are directly readable:

```{r}
#| label: movers
movers <- c(
  "Lincoln Riley",
  "Brian Kelly",
  "Kalen DeBoer",
  "Lane Kiffin",
  "Steve Sarkisian",
  "Mario Cristobal",
  "Josh Heupel",
  "Jimbo Fisher"
)
mover_detail <- pos_links |>
  filter(coach_name %in% movers) |>
  group_by(coach_name, team) |>
  summarise(
    draftees = n(),
    first_class = min(year),
    last_class = max(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(draftees))
mover_detail |>
  kable(
    caption = "Draftees by school for selected multi-school coaches, 2014 classes on. First and last draft class with a draftee under that coach at that school."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: movers-fig
#| fig-height: 8
p_mov <- ggplot(mover_detail, aes(y = reorder(team, draftees), x = draftees)) +
  geom_col_interactive(
    aes(
      tooltip = sprintf(
        "%s at %s: %d draftees, classes %d to %d",
        coach_name,
        team,
        draftees,
        first_class,
        last_class
      ),
      data_id = team
    ),
    fill = "#1b4f8a"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~coach_name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Kelly's total splits evenly; Kiffin's piles up at Ole Miss",
    subtitle = "Draftees per school for coaches who ran more than one program",
    x = "Draftees",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Last-school rule, 2014 classes on."
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p_mov, width_svg = 14, height_svg = 8)
```

Brian Kelly's 70 draftees divide into 44 at Notre Dame and 26 at LSU, and
Lincoln Riley lands close to even, 24 at Oklahoma and 16 at USC. Kalen
DeBoer's total sits at 17 draftees in two Alabama classes, against 10 at
Washington and 1 at Fresno State. Lane Kiffin's Ole Miss total, 25, is
many times his 3 at Florida Atlantic and 3 at USC, the pattern that
motivates the coach-versus-program followup.

```{r}
#| label: movers-pin
stopifnot(
  n_distinct(mover_detail$team[mover_detail$coach_name == "Kalen DeBoer"]) == 3,
  mover_detail$draftees[
    mover_detail$coach_name == "Brian Kelly" &
      mover_detail$team == "Notre Dame"
  ] ==
    44,
  mover_detail$draftees[
    mover_detail$coach_name == "Lincoln Riley" &
      mover_detail$team == "Oklahoma"
  ] ==
    24,
  mover_detail$draftees[
    mover_detail$coach_name == "Lane Kiffin" &
      mover_detail$team == "Ole Miss"
  ] ==
    25
)
```

### The rising transfer rate drives the disagreement

A transferred draftee has more pre-draft schools, which multiplies the
coach set under the every-season rule while leaving the last-school rule
untouched. Here a draftee counts as transferred when their pre-draft
roster seasons span more than one team, a broad definition that also
catches older data quirks.

```{r}
#| label: transfers
pool_teams <- pool |>
  group_by(year, overall) |>
  summarise(n_teams = n_distinct(team), .groups = "drop")
dat <- ovl |>
  left_join(pool_teams, by = c("year", "overall")) |>
  mutate(transferred = n_teams > 1)
xfer_share <- dat |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(share = mean(transferred), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#| label: transfer-figs
#| fig-height: 6
grp_fig <- dat |>
  filter(year >= 2014) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(transferred, "Transferred", "One school")) |>
  group_by(year, group) |>
  summarise(ident = mean(ovl == 1), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
p1 <- ggplot(grp_fig, aes(year, ident, color = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Transferred draftees rarely name the same coach set",
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Picks naming the same coach set\nunder both rules"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
p2 <- ggplot(xfer_share, aes(year, share)) +
  geom_line_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = sprintf("%d: %.0f%%", year, 100 * share), group = 1),
    linewidth = 1.1,
    color = "#1b4f8a"
  ) +
  geom_point_interactive(
    aes(tooltip = sprintf("%d: %.0f%%", year, 100 * share)),
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)) +
  labs(
    title = "The transfer share keeps climbing",
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Draftees whose pre-draft seasons span\nmore than one team"
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p1, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6)
girafe(ggobj = p2, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6)
```

Holding each class's identical-coach-set share within the transferred and
one-school groups fixed while returning the transfer share to its 2014
through 2023 mean tests whether the transfer climb accounts for the slide.

*Expecting the rising transfer share to account for the late slide.*

```{r}
#| label: counterfactual
grp <- dat |>
  group_by(year, transferred) |>
  summarise(ident = mean(ovl == 1), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
stayers <- grp |>
  filter(!transferred) |>
  transmute(year, keep_ident = ident, keep_n = n)
movers <- grp |>
  filter(transferred) |>
  transmute(year, xfer_ident = ident, xfer_n = n)
dec <- full_join(stayers, movers, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    share = coalesce(xfer_n, 0) / (coalesce(xfer_n, 0) + keep_n),
    actual = (coalesce(xfer_n, 0) * xfer_ident + keep_n * keep_ident) /
      (coalesce(xfer_n, 0) + keep_n)
  )
base_share <- mean(dec$share[dec$year >= 2014 & dec$year <= 2023])
dec <- dec |>
  mutate(
    if_xfer_frozen = base_share *
      coalesce(xfer_ident, keep_ident) +
      (1 - base_share) * keep_ident
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: counterfactual-fig
#| fig-height: 6
cf <- dec |>
  filter(year >= 2014) |>
  select(year, actual, if_xfer_frozen) |>
  pivot_longer(
    actual:if_xfer_frozen,
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "agreement"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    series = recode(
      series,
      actual = "Actual",
      if_xfer_frozen = "Transfer share frozen at the 2014 to 2023 mean"
    )
  )
p3 <- ggplot(cf, aes(year, agreement, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = window_mean, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Freeze the transfer rate and the slide disappears",
    subtitle = "Identical-coach-set share, actual and with the transfer rate held fixed",
    x = "Draft class",
    y = "Picks naming the same coach set\nunder both rules",
    caption = "Dashed line: 2014 and later mean from the window figure."
  ) +
  theme_cfb2nfl()
girafe(ggobj = p3, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6)
```

```{r}
#| label: transfer-pin
stopifnot(
  max(xfer_share$share[xfer_share$year <= 2013]) < 0.02,
  max(xfer_share$share[xfer_share$year == 2026]) > 0.45,
  tail(dec$if_xfer_frozen[dec$year >= 2024], 1) >
    mean(dec$actual[dec$year >= 2014 & dec$year <= 2023])
)
```

✅ Holds: with the transfer share returned to its 2014 through 2023 mean,
the identical-coach-set share for the classes of 2024 through 2026 climbs
back to the level of those earlier classes, while the actual series keeps
sliding.

## 4. Summary

Counting a draftee's head coaches is two different questions, not one. The
last-school rule names whoever finished the college career; the
every-season rule names everyone who oversaw part of it. For the classes
of 2014 through 2026 the two answers coincide for barely more than half of
picks on average, and below half in the three most recent classes. The
transfer boom accounts for most of the slide: held at its 2014 through
2023 level, the transfer share would have kept the two rules agreeing
about as often as they used to. The totals themselves are coach-level
counts that span schools, mix position groups unevenly, and, for coaches
who changed jobs, bundle several programs into one number.

## 5. Discussion

::: {.callout-important}
The two counting rules answer different questions and neither is the right
one in the abstract.

- The last-school rule names whoever finished a draftee's college career;
  the every-season rule names everyone who oversaw part of it.
- Nearly half of recent picks name a different coach set depending on which
  question is being asked, so any coach ranking built on draft picks owes
  the reader its counting rule.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
A head coach is associated with a draftee, not solely responsible for him.

- CFBD records head coaches only: no assistant coaches, no coordinators, no
  strength staff.
- The true apprenticeship picture, the Saban tree of coordinators who became
  head coaches, cannot be built from this source, and doing it would mean
  finding one that does.
:::

Several caveats bound these numbers.

- The window starts with the class of 2011 and the head-to-head uses classes
  of 2014 and later, so coaches whose draftees came mostly earlier are
  invisible here.
- The transfer flag is broad, spanning any multi-team pre-draft career
  rather than portal-era transfers specifically.
- Draftees are a selected group: they come disproportionately from programs
  that recruit well, so coach-level counts conflate the coach with the
  program until a recruiting control or a same-coach-different-school
  comparison is added. Those extensions are queued as followups.
